column2: The system of republican bureaucracy perpetuated by the Jacobins stems from the legacy of the pre-Event French Republic, which, as a unitary state, was divided into a series of administrative units: regions, departments, arrondissements, cantons, and communes. This system of government is characterized by a strict hierarchy at each administrative level and a lack of strict division between nobility and peasantry.

The origins of the Constitutional Church sometimes date back to events before the Event. While the Jacobins had just risen against the King of France, some bishops supported them and their Civil Constitution of the Clergy. After the Event, the Jacobins long sought to eradicate Catholicism in the territories they controlled, until the Catholic Bishop of Orleans decided to break communion with Rome and offered the Jacobins an agreement under which they would allow licensed Catholicism to operate in their territory in exchange for liturgical and doctrinal concessions. This agreement resulted in the creation of the Parisian obedience, which claims to be the rightful Bishop of Rome.
